source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 6 (The Bengal School and Cultural Nationalism).

sections.heading: 1. Colonial Art and the Reaction
points: In the 19th century, British-run **art schools** taught **Western academic (naturalistic/oil)** styles; **Raja Ravi Varma** popularised European realism with Indian (mythological) themes.
A nationalist reaction sought to revive **Indian identity in art** → the **Bengal School**.
This linked art to the **Swadeshi and nationalist movement (cultural nationalism)**.

sections.heading: 2. The Bengal School
points: **E.B. Havell** (principal of the Calcutta School of Art) and **Abanindranath Tagore** led the revival, drawing on **Mughal, Rajput, Ajanta and Far Eastern (Japanese wash)** traditions.
**Abanindranath Tagore** — the father of the Bengal School; famous work **'Bharat Mata'** (an iconic nationalist image).
Style: **soft 'wash technique', lyrical, spiritual, Indian themes** — a rejection of Western academic realism.

sections.heading: 3. Artists of the Bengal School
points: **Nandalal Bose** — a leading figure; associated with **Santiniketan (Kala Bhavana)**; designed illustrations for the Constitution.
**Asit Kumar Haldar, Kshitindranath Majumdar, Sunayani Devi**.
The Japanese artists **Okakura and Taikan** influenced the wash technique.
The movement spread nationalist and spiritual ideals through art.

sections.heading: 4. Significance
points: The Bengal School gave India a **distinct modern artistic identity** rooted in tradition.
It was closely tied to **cultural nationalism** and the freedom movement.
It paved the way for later modern Indian art (which later moved beyond it).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Raja Ravi Varma = European realism + Indian mythological themes.
Bengal School = revival of Indian art (E.B. Havell + Abanindranath Tagore).
Abanindranath Tagore = 'Bharat Mata'; father of the Bengal School.
Style = wash technique (Japanese influence), lyrical, spiritual.
Nandalal Bose = Santiniketan; illustrated the Constitution.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Abanindranath Tagore** painted **'Bharat Mata'** and led the Bengal School.
**Raja Ravi Varma** used **European academic (oil) realism** for Indian themes.
The Bengal School used the **wash technique** (Japanese influence).
**Nandalal Bose** illustrated the **original Constitution of India** (Santiniketan).
